source.title: From Latents to Labels: Zero-Shot Named Entity Recognition using Sparse Autoencoder Features
source.authors: Nakanyseth Vuth; Gilles Sérasset; Didier Schwab

record.tranche_reason: The paper builds SAE-NER on the premise that SAE features are monosemantic, but its reported experiments evaluate NER performance rather than whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: No result directly measures or tests individual-neuron polysemanticity. The appendix's feature ablations measure effects on entity typing after removing mapped SAE features; these do not test whether neurons have mixed or coherent meanings. NER performance and silver-data results are outside the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes dense neurons are polysemantic due to superposition (citing Bricken et al., Elhage et al.) and SAE features are monosemantic, then reports only its SAE-NER method's entity-typing and NER performance against probing baselines. No neuron polysemanticity rate, cause, or measurement choice is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that monosemantic SAE features give a training-free entity-typing signal that is superior to dense representations, especially in the biomedical domain. They find that targeted ablations indicate entity knowledge distributed across specialized features. They also conclude that SAE-NER silver data helps in cold-start settings but is limited by span-generation recall, with false negatives the most harmful noise. Neuron polysemanticity is assumed, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The study maps sparse autoencoder features to entity labels and evaluates NER; it does not reproduce neuron visualization or SoLU methods. The study relies on the monosemantic-feature premise for a different task.
record.method_sensitivity: NER performance varies with layer, model size, domain, dictionary width, and span-generation method; these are not measurements of polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted ablation of mapped SAE features gives class-specific entity-typing drops (e.g. -0.58 F1 for TIME at 50%). Random 20% ablation gives a drop under 0.005 F1. Ablating 20% removes about half the effect of ablating 50%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity-type information in Gemma-2-9B SAE features is distributed across multiple class-specific features rather than concentrated in one feature.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-NER entity typing outperforms dense-activation MLP probes, especially on biomedical AnEM (0.623 vs 0.421 F1). The authors attribute this to SAEs disentangling concepts hidden in polysemantic dense representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse SAE features of Gemma-2 provide a better zero-shot entity-typing signal than dense activations with supervised probes.

record.peer_reviewed: Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
record.problems: The study does not directly analyze individual neurons or test mixed-input responses. Its claim-relevant premise about monosemantic SAE features is assumed rather than evaluated. The feature-ablation results concern entity-typing performance, not polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were reported. NER typing, full-pipeline, silver-data, and noise-perturbation results were not extracted because they do not measure neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No vision models or image-classifier neurons examined.
No share or layer-wise rate of polysemantic MLP neurons in language models measured. Polysemanticity of Gemma-2 dense states is asserted, not measured.
Superposition is cited as background only. No test of capacity pressure as the cause.
No initialization, regularization or training-noise conditions tested.
No variation of activation function, architecture or regularization affecting polysemantic neuron share.
No polysemanticity measure varied by activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The record's classification as T4 / uses_without_test is correct; one could also argue for 'assumes'. Monosemanticity of SAE features is explicitly assumed in the method section: 'We assume that an ideal SAE feature is monosemantic.' No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No InceptionV1 neuron or other image-classifier neuron is examined.
No share of polysemantic MLP neurons, token/context responses, or layer-wise rates is measured.
Superposition is invoked as background, but the study does not test whether feature capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons.
No initialization, regularization, training-noise, or capacity-sufficient condition is tested for neuron polysemanticity.
The study compares SAE-based NER configurations, not polysemantic-neuron shares across activations, architectures, or regularization settings.
No canonical mixed neuron is reinterpreted or tested for a shared feature or related offshoots.
No neuron polysemanticity measurement is varied by activation range or explanation-scoring method.

rows.subject: M9^131k (Gemma-2-9B SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed mapped SAE features for each entity type, removing the top 50% for the target type.
rows.baseline: without ablation; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: Class-specific sharp drops; TIME: -0.58 F1; other entity types virtually unaffected.
rows.note: This is an ablation of SAE features used for entity typing, not an ablation or measurement of individual-neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Measures the effect of ablating the study's own mapped SAE features on entity-typing F1. This is a method validation, not a measure of neuron polysemanticity. Linking to none is correct.

rows.subject: M9^131k (Gemma-2-9B SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top 20% of mapped SAE features for each entity type; compared its impact with the 50% ablation.
rows.measure: Entity-typing F1 impact relative to the 50% targeted ablation
rows.baseline: 50% targeted ablation; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Ablating 20% of features removes roughly half the performance of ablating 50%.
rows.note: The paper uses this comparison to support a distributed representation of entity knowledge across specialized SAE features.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method under 20% vs 50% ablation. It bears on distributed representation across SAE features, not on polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: M9^131k (Gemma-2-9B SAE)
rows.operation_detail: Randomly removed 20% of mapped SAE features as a control ablation.
rows.baseline: without ablation; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: < 0.005 drop in F1; described as negligible.
rows.note: This control concerns the effect of removing SAE features on entity typing, not neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Random-ablation control for the study's own method. No bearing on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
